clue.text: Base for drilling hole in the wall behind hollow panel

indicators.note: the drilled cash machine comes after, i.e. behind, the hollowed panel
a hollow panel has only its shell left, so just the outer letters of the word are kept
the little word for bores through the cash machine, ending up inside it

parts.note: a hole in the wall is the informal British name for a cash machine, an ATM

explanation.surface: A rig worker describes boring through a wall behind a panel to set up a drilling base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base for drilling' reads as one phrase, but 'for' is a piece of the wordplay, and 'drilling' is the insertion signal; 'hole in the wall' is British slang for a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised level surface on which something stands is a base, as in an oil-drilling rig's deck.

clue.text: One swimming in location without current

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for location goes round the current symbol

parts.note: a location is a place
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is swimming in a spot where there is no current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The flatfish is a sea creature, so it is literally one that swims.

clue.text: He may thread line through needle

indicators.note: the line letter runs through the middle of the word for needle

parts.note: to needle someone is to irritate them; as a noun, needle is irritation or anger

explanation.surface: Someone threads a line through the eye of a needle, like a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sewing, but the threading is of fishing line; needle is anger, not a sewing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman threads line through rod rings and hooks, so 'he' stands for that person.

clue.text: Football Association will attempt to protect right to be inadequate

parts.note: FA is the abbreviation for the Football Association, English football's governing body
will contracted is 'll, as in he'll

indicators.note: the attempt wraps around the right letter as if guarding it

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, as in have a shot

explanation.surface: The football authorities will try to shield a right that proves inadequate.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up short of a target is to be insufficient or inadequate.

clue.text: Moving picture range is improving following complaint

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges the two words together

explanation.surface: A cinema film's range of quality is getting better after criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving picture' reads as a film, but 'Moving' is the anagram signal on PICTURE and RANGE together; 'complaint' is an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting well after an illness is recovering health, so the definition is a synonym.

clue.text: Fish courses are available here

definitions.meaning: a group of fish swimming together is a shoal or ...
a place offering lessons or courses of study, such as a college

explanation.surface: A fish restaurant advertising its menu courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a collective noun for fish, and an institution where courses are taught.

clue.text: Animal from Channel Islands eating grass

indicators.note: the islands' letters take the grass inside them, as if swallowing it

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey
oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: An animal from Jersey or Guernsey is grazing on grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Jersey cow; the creature is in fact South American.
explanation.definitionFit: This raccoon relative from the Americas is a specific example of an animal.

clue.text: Material in newspaper perhaps leads to demonstrations in England

parts.note: a newspaper is an example of an organ, a publication voicing a group's views

indicators.note: the leads of the words are their opening letters, one from each

explanation.surface: A newspaper's coverage sparks protest marches across England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine, stiff, transparent muslin is a kind of fabric, so it is an example of material.

clue.text: Bridge opponents object following card game's unresolved issue

indicators.note: the bridge and object pieces come after the card game

parts.note: loo is an old card game; the possessive just links it to what follows
in bridge South and East sit on opposing sides, giving the compass letters S and E
an end is an object or aim, as in to that end

explanation.surface: At the card table, bridge rivals raise an objection after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South partner against East-West, so S and E are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unfinished or not tied up is an idiomatic unresolved matter.

clue.text: Heavenly whiff of aromatic plant

parts.note: heavenly and angelic both describe beings of heaven

indicators.note: only a whiff, a tiny trace, of the word is taken: its first letter

explanation.surface: A divine scent comes from a fragrant plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic herb, whose candied stems decorate cakes, is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Lurid tone of old gay novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book reviewer describes the garish colouring of a vintage gay novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal on OLD GAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name for fluorescent paint has come to mean any glaringly bright colour.

clue.text: He fobs off a mate of Tom's before her arrival's been noted

indicators.note: the cat's mate comes before the jumbled letters

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and a female cat is a queen

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man brushes off a tomcat's mate before her coming has been registered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' means set to music: Handel wrote The Arrival of the Queen of Sheba.
explanation.definitionFit: Her entrance was famously set to music by Handel, so it has literally been put into notes.

clue.text: Struggle to find mate in black and white musical

definitions.text: Struggle to find mate in black and white
definitions.meaning: a contest to deliver checkmate on a board of black and white squares
the stage musical by Benny Andersson, Björn Ulvaeus and Tim Rice

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to find a partner in a black and white musical film.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game ends in checkmate on black and white squares, and a 1980s stage show shares its name.

clue.text: Caution daughter turning to religious teaching's unhealthy interest in sex

indicators.note: the daughter letter turns into, i.e. is exchanged for, the religious teaching letters

parts.note: prudence is caution or care
RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: A cautious daughter turns to religion, which is a sort of prurient interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurience is excessive or lewd preoccupation with sexual matters.

clue.text: Telling on bad person who's worse than the rest

definitions.text: person who's worse than the rest

indicators.note: in an across answer, on places the telling after the bad piece

parts.note: poor means bad, of low quality
a relation is a telling, as in the relation of a story

explanation.surface: Someone informing on a bad person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling on' looks like informing; 'on' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the weakest or least valued member of a group, compared with the others.

clue.text: A man upset about a French actor's name

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on history
un is the French for a

explanation.surface: A man is upset about a French actor's name being mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actor' means one who acts, not a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun such as driver or teacher names a doer, the one performing the verb's action.

clue.text: Rebel when a repressive regime purges undesirables

indicators.note: purges means gets rid of, so the pests are removed

parts.note: a police state is a repressive regime
lice are unwanted pests

explanation.surface: A dissident rebels when an authoritarian government purges undesirable people.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing LICE from A POLICE STATE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who abandons a faith or cause is a renegade, so a type of rebel.

clue.text: Incoherent means of removing barriers to conspicuous wealth

parts.note: a battering ram is used to break down gates or doors
bling is showy jewellery or flashy displays of money

explanation.surface: An incoherent rant about breaking down barriers that protect the rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that wanders aimlessly is disjointed and hard to follow, so lacking coherence.

clue.text: Nice portrait represented someone doing something

indicators.note: re-presented, presented again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasing portrait shows a person busy at some activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner is one who actively practises a craft or profession, i.e. who does it.

clue.text: Fundamental thing in favour of not getting upset

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone supports a fundamental principle without getting upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle in the nucleus is one of matter's fundamental components.

clue.text: Cuba's bothered about America — you can count on it

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, i.e. around, the America letter
bothered means disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cuba is upset with America, a country you can rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bothered' scrambles CUBAS into ABCUS, which goes about A.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of sliding beads is a counting tool, so one literally counts on it.

clue.text: Back reasonable work accommodating barrister's initial demands for evidence

indicators.note: back means turn around, so the whole assembly is read backwards

parts.note: sane means sensible, reasonable

indicators.note: the word for work takes in the barrister's letter, housing it

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music

indicators.note: the initial of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Supporting a reasonable piece of work that houses a lawyer's opening demands for evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like support; it reverses SANE plus OPBUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Writs requiring a witness to attend court or produce documents are demands for testimony.

clue.text: This venue is going to promote poetry

indicators.note: in a down answer, promoting the poem puts it above the other piece

parts.note: an ode is a poem
on means taking place or going, as in the show is on

explanation.surface: A venue announces it will promote poetry readings.
explanation.definitionFit: This chain of cinemas is a well-known British entertainment venue.

clue.text: This pulse is cooked to make broth

indicators.note: cooked as in cooked up or falsified, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lentil or bean is cooked to make soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a bean or lentil; it is a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhythmic beat of the heart is a pulse.

clue.text: Lives in near chaos come into being

indicators.note: the lives piece goes in the middle of the jumbled letters
the word is thrown into chaos, its letters jumbled

parts.note: is means exists or lives, as in there is life

explanation.surface: Lives in near chaos have emerged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' reads as a plural noun but is the verb, and 'chaos' is the anagram signal on 'near', giving AREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Having emerged or appeared is the past participle of the verb to arise.

clue.text: German at risk of involuntary movement associated with old age

parts.note: on means at stake, as money bet on a horse
a tic is an involuntary muscle twitch

explanation.surface: A German at risk of a twitch associated with old age.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective, from the Greek for old man, relates to the elderly and ageing.

clue.text: Article in Der Spiegel about new German locomotive

indicators.note: the article goes about, i.e. around, the new and German letters

parts.note: eine is a German indefinite article, the kind found in the magazine Der Spiegel

explanation.surface: An article in the German magazine about a new German locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: The engine is the self-propelled vehicle that pulls a train, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Pay studs perhaps to abandon resistance to a little nookie

indicators.note: one resistance letter is abandoned and replaced

parts.note: studs are an example of earrings
R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: only a little of the word is taken, its first letter

explanation.surface: Studs, perhaps, give up their resistance in exchange for a bit of nookie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studs' suggests womanisers, but they are ear jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Money received for work is income, the same as wages or pay.
